subject.title: [Bug]: Sandbox container exits immediately when no-new-privileges is applied (exec /usr/bin/sleep: operation not permitted)

question: Should OpenClaw add an explicit way to run Docker sandboxes without `no-new-privileges` on incompatible hosts, or should it keep failing closed and only improve diagnostics?
rationale: The remaining fix is not just mechanical: omitting or retrying without `no-new-privileges` restores affected hosts but weakens a sandbox hardening control, while keeping it unconditional preserves the boundary but leaves these hosts unable to use Docker sandboxes.

options.title: Add explicit dangerous opt-out
options.body: Keep `no-new-privileges` enabled by default, add a clearly named opt-out with security audit/doctor/status warnings, docs, tests, and real Docker proof on the affected path.

options.title: Improve fail-closed diagnostics only
options.body: Keep the hardening flag unconditional and surface a clear EPERM/no-new-privileges diagnosis with guidance to change Docker/runtime/backend instead of weakening sandbox options.

options.title: Automatic fallback retry
options.body: Retry container creation without the flag after the specific EPERM failure, accepting a less explicit security downgrade that must be carefully reported and tested.

recommendation.title: Add explicit dangerous opt-out
recommendation.body: Keep `no-new-privileges` enabled by default, add a clearly named opt-out with security audit/doctor/status warnings, docs, tests, and real Docker proof on the affected path.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent sandbox Docker changes plus the security-sensitive owner boundary make this the best available routing candidate from current history.
